claims.text: Social media engagement is associated with higher levels of anxiety.
Social media engagement is associated with higher levels of voyeurism.
Social media engagement is associated with higher levels of exhibitionism.
Higher levels of anxiety, voyeurism, and exhibitionism increase Fear of Missing Out (FoMO).
Psychological strain associated with FoMO leads to compulsive social media use.

evidence.description: A 30-item quantitative survey of 108 children showed social media engagement is associated with higher levels of anxiety.
Survey results from 108 children showed social media engagement is associated with higher levels of voyeurism.
Survey findings from 108 children demonstrated an association between social media engagement and higher levels of exhibitionism.
Quantitative analysis of 108 survey responses found that anxiety, voyeurism, and exhibitionism increase FoMO.
Survey results indicated that psychological strain results in compulsive social media use among children.

methodologies.name: Quantitative Survey Administration
methodologies.description: A 30-item survey administered to children to analyze the relationships between social media engagement, anxiety, voyeurism, exhibitionism, FoMO, and compulsive use.
